d: A bodice block (bodice sloper) drafted with the classic British Bray method

chestEase.d: How much ease to add at the bust line. The book drafts 10 cm, of which shaping the waist takes back a few centimetres

seatEase.d: How much ease to add at the hip line. The book drafts 6 cm, and puts all of it on the front panel

waistEase.d: How much ease to leave at the waist before the darts are shaped. The book allows 3 to 6 cm on the full pattern

waistFit.d: Whether to shape the waist with center-line slant, side-seam intake and darts, or to leave the plain block with its simple side-seam taper

backWidthPct.d: The across-back width, as a fraction of the chest measurement. Round-shouldered figures need more, erect figures less

chestWidthPct.d: The across-chest width, as a fraction of the chest measurement. It moves opposite to the back width as posture changes

bustDartWidth.d: How wide the shoulder/bust dart is where it opens on the shoulder seam, as a fraction of the chest measurement

armholeBridgeBonus.d: How much wider to make the armhole bridge, the span between the back-width and chest-width lines, as a fraction of the chest measurement. The book's preferred way to enlarge a small armhole, but only where a wider armhole is obtainable: it spends chest ease. Leave it at zero and the underarm is deepened instead
